title: Drake — 2yo Aylesbury: laboured breathing and a change in voice
presentation: Two-year-old Aylesbury drake, three weeks of gradually worsening breathing, now open-mouthed after any exertion, with a hoarse, weak call. Housed in a damp straw-bedded shed over winter.

stages.title: Examine the bird
stages.briefing: Weight 3.1 kg, BCS 2/5, keel prominent. RR 44/min with open-mouth breathing after handling, tail bobbing. Voice hoarse. Auscultation over the trachea: harsh referred noise; over the caudal air sacs: increased sounds on the right. Mucous membranes pink. Housing: damp, mouldy straw, poor ventilation, litter unchanged for six weeks.
stages.prompt: Which findings point to lower airway or air sac disease?

options.label: Tail bobbing with open-mouth breathing after minimal exertion
options.detail: Increased respiratory effort in a bird

options.label: Asymmetric increase in caudal air sac sounds
options.detail: Focal, not diffuse, disease

options.label: Three weeks of progression with weight loss
options.detail: A chronic, consuming process

options.label: Damp, mouldy straw with poor ventilation
options.detail: The exposure — but it is history, not a clinical sign

options.label: Pink mucous membranes
options.detail: Reassuring, and it does not localise

stages.explanation: Birds have no diaphragm, so tail bobbing and open-mouth breathing after trivial exertion mark significant respiratory compromise. The asymmetry is the useful physical finding — it says focal granulomatous disease rather than diffuse infection. A hoarse voice adds a syringeal lesion to the picture, which is precisely where aspergillosis likes to sit.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: The drake tolerates brief handling. Radiography, endoscopy and laboratory submission are all available.

options.label: Whole-body radiographs including a lateral view of the air sacs
options.detail: Air sac thickening, focal densities, syringeal mass

options.label: Endoscopy of the trachea, syrinx and air sacs with biopsy
options.detail: Direct visualisation and a sample of the lesion

options.label: Cytology and fungal culture of the lesion or a tracheal wash
options.detail: Hyphae seen, and the organism named

options.label: Haematology with a protein electrophoresis
options.detail: Monocytosis and beta-globulin rise support aspergillosis

options.label: Aspergillus galactomannan or antibody testing
options.detail: Supportive when imaging and cytology agree

options.label: Chlamydia psittaci PCR alone as the diagnosis
options.detail: Worth screening, but it will not explain a focal air sac mass

options.label: Blood lead concentration
options.detail: Sensible in a waterfowl with neurological signs, not with focal air sac disease

stages.explanation: Aspergillosis is diagnosed by seeing it: endoscopy with biopsy and cytology beats any serological test, and the serology is only worth interpreting alongside the images. Radiographs first tells you where to put the scope. The haematology and electrophoresis are supportive evidence that also grades how chronic this is.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Radiographs: thickened right caudal thoracic air sac wall with a focal soft tissue density; hyperinflation of the left air sacs. Endoscopy: white-to-green plaques on the right caudal air sac and a granuloma narrowing the syrinx. Cytology of the plaque: septate branching hyphae with mixed inflammatory cells. Fungal culture: Aspergillus fumigatus. Haematology: white cell count 28 ×10⁹/L with monocytosis; protein electrophoresis shows a raised beta-globulin fraction. Chlamydia PCR negative.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Chronic granulomatous aspergillosis of the air sacs and syrinx
options.detail: Hyphae on cytology with A. fumigatus cultured from a visible plaque

options.label: The syringeal granuloma explains the voice change and the effort
options.detail: A mass narrowing the airway at the syrinx

options.label: Mouldy bedding in poor ventilation is the likely source
options.detail: A heavy environmental spore load

options.label: Chlamydiosis is excluded
options.detail: PCR negative

options.label: The monocytosis proves a bacterial infection
options.detail: Monocytosis is expected in avian granulomatous fungal disease

options.label: This is likely to resolve on antibiotics alone
options.detail: Antibacterials have no effect on Aspergillus

stages.explanation: Culture alone would leave doubt — Aspergillus grows from plenty of samples it has merely contaminated — but hyphae in an inflammatory exudate taken from a plaque you can see makes it the disease. The syringeal lesion is what ties the hoarse voice to the breathlessness, and it is also what makes the prognosis guarded rather than fair.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Focal air sac plaques with a syringeal granuloma, septate branching hyphae on cytology, Aspergillus fumigatus cultured, monocytosis with raised beta-globulins, mouldy bedding, Chlamydia negative.

options.label: Chronic aspergillosis of the caudal air sacs and syrinx from environmental exposure
options.detail: Confirmed fungal granulomas with their source

options.label: Bacterial air sacculitis
options.detail: Cytology and culture identify a fungus

options.label: Chlamydiosis
options.detail: PCR negative and the lesions are granulomatous fungal

options.label: Tracheal foreign body
options.detail: Endoscopy showed a granuloma, not a foreign body

options.label: Cardiac disease with pulmonary oedema
options.detail: Does not produce air sac plaques or hyphae

stages.explanation: Naming aspergillosis sets a long, expensive and uncertain treatment course — itraconazole or voriconazole with nebulised therapy, possibly debulking the syringeal granuloma — and it changes the shed before it changes the bird: dry, dust-free bedding and real ventilation, or the next duck presents the same way.
